title: Check the engine version at client startup
summary: Whenever the client is about to call the engine, it first verifies the engine: a missing engine produces a message that names the engine and the concrete install command, an engine below the declared minimum produces a message that names the required version and the concrete upgrade command, and a compatible engine proceeds normally. Reporting the client's own version and the declared requirement is exempt from this check and works without an engine, so a bare `executable not found` failure is never the outcome of a command that needs the engine.
requirements: The client declares exactly one minimum supported engine version; the value it shows the user is the same value it enforces before using the engine, and no user-controlled option or setting lowers, skips or overrides it.

Asking the client for its own version reports the client version together with the declared minimum supported engine version, ends successfully, works on a machine with no engine installed, and contacts no engine.
The client's usage help is produced and ends successfully on a machine with no engine installed, and contacts no engine.
Reporting the client's version and printing usage help are the only surfaces exempt from engine confirmation; every other client operation confirms the engine before doing anything else.

Before the client first uses the engine in an invocation it confirms that the engine is present and asks the engine the version it reports about itself, and carries that result through the rest of the invocation.
The engine's version is asked at most once per invocation.
After a failed confirmation the invocation makes no further request to the engine and does not attempt the requested work.

When the engine cannot be found or cannot be started, the invocation fails with one message that names the engine, states that the client requires it, and contains one line that installs a current engine and can be copied and run unchanged; the low-level system error text is never the only thing the user sees.

When the engine reports a version below the declared minimum, the invocation fails with one message that names the required minimum version, the version found, and one line that installs a newer engine and can be copied and run unchanged; the requested work is not attempted.

When the engine answers but no version can be confirmed from its answer, the invocation fails in the same actionable shape as the too-old case: it states that compatibility could not be confirmed, names the required minimum version and carries the line that installs a newer engine; the requested work is not attempted.

The installation line carried by every failure message is one complete line that a user can copy and run unchanged; the same line serves the missing and the too-old case because running it installs a current engine in either situation.

Versions compare as sequences of numeric components, numerically, one component at a time from the first; a version with fewer components equals the same version with trailing zero components; a leading version marker and any non-numeric suffix after the numeric components do not affect the outcome; a larger later component counts as newer even when its text is longer; the declared minimum is an inclusive lower bound.

When the engine reports the declared minimum or a newer version, the requested operation behaves exactly as before: the same requests reach the engine, the human-readable and structured output is unchanged, and the outcome is unchanged.
The client never installs, upgrades or otherwise modifies the engine; every failure path only reports what the user can do.

When the client reports a failure in its structured form, a missing engine and a not-compatible engine each appear as exactly one reported failure carrying the same message as the plain form and a non-zero outcome, consistent with the client's other failures.

Starting the interactive session performs the same confirmation first; with a missing, too-old or unconfirmable engine the session prints the actionable message and ends with a non-zero outcome without opening a prompt.
acceptance: With no engine installed, asking the client for its version ends successfully and reports the client version together with the declared minimum engine version, contacting no engine. Check: review observes the version request on a machine without the engine and confirms the reported pair, the successful outcome and the absence of engine contact.

With no engine installed, the client's usage help is printed and ends successfully without contacting an engine. Check: review observes the help request on a machine without the engine and confirms the printed help, the successful outcome and the absence of engine contact.

An engine reporting a version one numeric component below the minimum shown by the version report is refused as too old, and an engine reporting exactly that shown minimum is accepted. Check: review observes both boundary cases against the value the version report shows.
No user-facing option or setting lowers, skips or overrides the enforced minimum. Check: review compares the shown and enforced values and inspects the client's options and settings.

An invocation that asks the engine for several things causes the engine's version to be asked at most once. Check: review observes such an invocation and counts the version questions the engine receives.

A failed confirmation leaves the engine with no request beyond the version question, whether the engine is too old or reports no usable version. Check: review observes both failure cases and confirms that no operation request followed.
Every operation covered by the confirmation asks the engine about its version before any other request. Check: review observes the order of the requests such an operation makes to the engine.

With no engine installed, an operation that needs the engine fails and prints one message that names the engine, says the client requires it, and contains a single installation line that can be copied and run unchanged; the low-level system error is not what the user sees alone. Check: review reads the message produced without an engine.

With an engine older than the declared minimum, an operation fails and prints one message naming the required minimum, the version found and a single installation line, with no work attempted. Check: review reads the message produced against an older engine and confirms that no work was attempted.

With an engine that answers but reports no usable version, the operation fails in the same actionable shape, names the required minimum and carries the installation line. Check: review reads the message produced against an engine that reports no version and compares its shape with the too-old message.
The installation lines shown in the failure messages are complete single lines that can be copied and run unchanged. Check: review judges the printed lines to be complete and runnable as printed.

An engine reporting 0.10.0 is accepted against a declared minimum of 0.9.0; an engine reporting 0.9.0 is accepted against a minimum of 0.9.0; a minimum reported with a non-numeric suffix or with trailing zero components is accepted as equal; a leading version marker changes nothing. Check: review observes each of these comparisons.

With an engine exactly at the declared minimum and with a newer engine, every operation and the interactive session behave as before: the same requests reach the engine, the same output appears and the outcome is unchanged. Check: review compares this behaviour with the behaviour that precedes the change.

The client never installs, upgrades or modifies the engine: after each failure path nothing is installed, and an engine that was present keeps its version and content. Check: review observes the engine's state after the missing-engine and too-old failure paths.

When the client reports in its structured form, a missing engine and an engine below the minimum each yield exactly one reported failure carrying the same message as the plain form and a non-zero outcome. Check: review observes both failures in the structured form and compares the message and the outcome with the plain form.

Starting the interactive session with no engine, or with an engine below the minimum, prints the actionable message and ends with a non-zero outcome without ever showing a prompt, and the engine receives no request beyond the version question. Check: review observes the session start against an absent and an older engine.
constraints: Only the client changes; the engine, the engine's installer and the version the engine reports stay as they are.
The client stays independent of the engine and never installs, upgrades or modifies it.
The declared minimum is a client-owned value chosen by the developer as the oldest engine that answers the client's needs; it is not a user setting.
Failures reuse the client's existing failure reporting conventions; no second failure shape is introduced.
The project's existing cross-repository verification remains the proof that the real engine and the real client work together; it is neither replaced nor relaxed.
The confirmation is exercised through the client's real startup path and is never bypassed.
User documentation and release notes are not updated here; the milestone plans them separately.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

external_dependencies.name: Forgel engine version self-report
external_dependencies.interface: The engine answers a question about the version it runs with one structured answer from which the running version can be read; an answer with no readable version counts as unconfirmed.
external_dependencies.docs: main repository README, engine command reference

external_dependencies.name: Forgel published installation guidance
external_dependencies.interface: A single published line installs a current engine together with the client, is safe to re-run when the client is already present, and is the line quoted verbatim in the failure messages.
external_dependencies.docs: main and code repositories, installation sections of their README files

result.summary: Completed and verified the engine-version confirmation at client startup. The client enforces a single declared minimum engine version (forgel_code/compat.py) that is the same value the version report shows; `--version` and help stay engine-free. Every other command and the interactive session confirm the engine once, ask for its version exactly once, and refuse a missing, too-old or unconfirmable engine before any operation request. Failure paths print one actionable English message naming the engine, the required minimum and the found version, with a single copy-pasteable install line, and reuse the existing plain/JSON failure reporting and non-zero exit codes. Version comparison follows the numeric-component rules. This session fixed the test doubles so they answer the version question: tests/stub_engine.py now defines the module-level ENGINE it referenced (the version answer previously raised NameError) and answers `version`/`--version` before replaying canned output, and tests/test_interactive.py's inline stub answers `version` and exports FORGEL_ENGINE so the real startup path reaches the stub. Verified with the repository gate `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 378 tests, OK.
assumptions: The stub engine doubles were corrected rather than the confirmation bypassed: the tests kept exercising the client's real startup path.
The install line uses the client's own version tag for the published install script, so running it installs a current engine and is safe to re-run in both the missing and the too-old case.
Version questions are answered by the engine's `version` command in the machine-readable form, matching the client's existing engine protocol.

review.summary: The attributed change wires the client's engine-version confirmation into both real startup paths: `forgel_code/cli.py` calls `compat.confirm(engine)` immediately before the first `engine.run(...)` of a one-shot command, and `forgel_code/interactive.py` performs the same confirmation before the interactive session is created, printing the actionable message and returning a non-zero outcome on failure instead of opening a prompt. The version-report and help surfaces stay outside the confirmation because `--version`/`--help` are handled by the parser before that call. The test stubs were adapted coherently: the subprocess stub engines now answer the version question (with a configurable version via `FORGEL_STUB_VERSION`), and the interactive session test sets `FORGEL_ENGINE` and stubs `version`. No test was removed or weakened by the diff; the edits add engine-version answers needed by the new startup request. The remaining substance — the declared minimum, the version report showing it, the version comparison rules and the actionable install/upgrade messages — lives in the pre-existing `compat`/`version_report` modules that this diff consumes (not attributed to this task), and the authoritative QA run (repository + environment tests, exit 0) exercises the client through these paths. I found no logical error, unrelated file, secret or weakened test in the attributed diff.

requirements.requirement: FR-1 One declared minimum engine version; shown value equals enforced value; no user option lowers or skips it
requirements.note: The diff adds no option or setting that alters the minimum; confirmation is invoked unconditionally from both startup paths. The single declared value is owned by the pre-existing compat/version_report code the diff calls.

requirements.requirement: FR-2 Version request reports client version plus minimum engine version, succeeds, works with no engine, contacts no engine
requirements.note: The confirmation is reached only after argument parsing succeeds; the `--version` surface is handled by the parser/`version_requested` path before `compat.confirm`, so no engine is spawned for it.

requirements.requirement: FR-3 Usage help is produced and succeeds with no engine, contacting no engine
requirements.note: Help is produced by argparse before the confirmation call in `cli.main`, so it cannot reach the engine.

requirements.requirement: FR-4 Only version and help are exempt; every other operation confirms the engine first
requirements.note: `compat.confirm(engine)` is called right before the first `engine.run` on the one-shot path and before the session opens on the interactive path; those two are the only entry points.

requirements.requirement: FR-5 Presence and self-reported version confirmed before first engine use and carried through the invocation
requirements.note: Confirmation precedes every `engine.run` on both paths; the engine object passed to `InteractiveSession` is the same object the confirmation ran against.

requirements.requirement: FR-6 Version asked at most once per invocation
requirements.note: Confirmation is invoked exactly once per path; the no-argument interactive dispatch is handled separately from the one-shot `try` block, so the session path does not confirm twice.

requirements.requirement: FR-7 After a failed confirmation no further engine request and no requested work
requirements.note: `compat.confirm` raises before `engine.run(arguments)` on the CLI path and before `InteractiveSession` is constructed on the session path.

requirements.requirement: FR-8 Missing/unstartable engine fails with one message naming the engine, stating the client requires it, carrying one pasteable install line
requirements.note: The failure propagates as the client's existing `EngineError` message; the wording and install line are produced by the pre-existing compat code the diff consumes.

requirements.requirement: FR-9 Too-old engine fails with one message naming required minimum, version found and one pasteable install line; no work attempted
requirements.note: Raised from `compat.confirm` before any operation request; the diff guarantees ordering.

requirements.requirement: FR-10 Unconfirmable version fails in the same actionable shape naming the minimum and carrying the install line; no work attempted
requirements.note: Same raise-and-return path; the diff treats every confirmation failure identically.

requirements.requirement: FR-11 Every failure message carries one complete pasteable line serving missing and too-old cases
requirements.note: No per-case message construction was added in the diff, so the single line comes from one shared source in the pre-existing compat code.

requirements.requirement: FR-12 Numeric component comparison, inclusive lower bound, trailing zeros, leading marker and suffix ignored
requirements.note: Comparison logic is not in the attributed diff; it is exercised by the repository and environment test runs that QA reports as passing.

requirements.requirement: FR-13 Compatible engine behaves exactly as before
requirements.note: The diff adds one confirmation call and no change to argument translation, rendering or exit handling; the stub engines were extended only to answer the new version question.

requirements.requirement: FR-14 Client never installs, upgrades or modifies the engine
requirements.note: The diff only calls the confirmation and prints the raised message; no install or upgrade command appears anywhere in the change.

requirements.requirement: FR-15 Structured form reports one failure with the plain message and non-zero outcome
requirements.note: The failure is raised inside the existing `try` in `cli.main`, so it flows through the existing `_report_failure` shape rather than a new one.

requirements.requirement: FR-16 Interactive session confirms first; missing, too-old or unconfirmable engine prints the message and exits non-zero without a prompt
requirements.note: `run()` confirms before constructing `InteractiveSession`, prints `exc.message` to stderr and returns `exc.returncode or 1`, so no prompt is reached.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: only the client changes; engine, installer and engine-reported version unchanged
requirements.note: Only `forgel_code/cli.py`, `forgel_code/interactive.py` and test stubs under `tests/` are touched; no engine code is modified.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: failures reuse existing failure conventions; no second failure shape
requirements.note: The new path raises the existing `EngineError` and, where relevant, flows through `_report_failure`; nothing new is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: cross-repository verification neither replaced nor relaxed
requirements.note: No verification harness change is present in the attributed diff.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: user-facing messages English; documentation and release notes not updated here
requirements.note: The only added user-visible text in the diff is a stderr print of the existing message; no documentation file is touched.

requirements.requirement: Change hygiene: only task-relevant files committed, no unrelated, temporary, debug or generated files
requirements.note: All six attributed files are the CLI, the interactive session and the three stub-based test modules the confirmation requires; no stray or generated artifact is present.

requirements.requirement: No weakened or deleted tests without justification
requirements.note: No test removal was detected and the diff only adds engine-version answers to the existing stubs plus `FORGEL_ENGINE` wiring in the session test.
